STEP 1 - Vessel type: The food sits on a white, square-ish flat plate with a rim band and flat centre, with no curved inner wall. Flat plate, square.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plates are typically 20-30 cm. This one looks like a standard dinner plate, so I estimate about 25 cm across.
b) Reference: the green beans are roughly 8-10 cm long, and the chicken pieces are about 5-6 cm across. The plate spans roughly 2.5 to 3 chicken-piece lengths... more usefully, the plate width is about 4-5 times the length of a green bean cluster, which is consistent with ~25 cm.
Final width: 25 cm (square), footprint = 25^2 = 625 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Breaded chicken pieces: two visible pieces (one larger wedge, one smaller piece), roughly 60-70 g each when cooked, so about 120 g total. Coating and light oil included.
- Green beans: a cluster covering roughly 20-25% of the plate's lower-left area, about 150 cm² footprint, about 1 cm thick when piled. Volume about 150 cm³ × bulk density 0.6 (cooked vegetables) ≈ 90 g, estimated at ~80 g.
- Caesar-style salad (cooked/dressed romaine with dressing and croutons/parmesan bits): covers roughly 200-220 cm² of the right side, about 2 cm thick as a mound, average about 1 cm. Volume ≈ 210 cm³; leafy greens with dressing at ~0.4 g/ml effective density ≈ 85 g. Dressing adds weight; estimate about 100 g total.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: No base layer beyond the salad and beans; the plate is a single flat layer, so no hidden items are added.

STEP 5 - Energy:
- Breaded chicken: about 240 kcal per 100 g (coating adds fat and carbs).
- Green beans, cooked: about 35 kcal per 100 g.
- Caesar salad with dressing: about 190 kcal per 100 g (dressing is calorie-dense).

Totals: chicken ≈ 120 g (≈ 290 kcal), beans ≈ 80 g (≈ 28 kcal), salad ≈ 100 g (≈ 190 kcal). Total about 500 g and roughly 510 kcal.
